strict.criterion: Mainstream school and university course materials are routinely delivered wirelessly to students' portable devices.
strict.rationale: Apple's 2007 iTunes U offered free supplemental university lectures, but ordinary K–12 and college curricula in 2009 still relied predominantly on printed textbooks and paper handouts. Wireless cloud delivery of core assignments, readings, and course portals became routine across schools during the 2010s and early 2020s.
changedConditions: Requires routine wireless delivery of core school/course materials rather than supplemental university podcasts

evidence.title: Apple: iTunes U opens on the iTunes Store
evidence.note: Free lectures and educational material from major universities; Wi-Fi-capable computers establish wireless access but not wireless prevalence at every school.

evidence.title: Wireless Internet Use — Pew Research Center
evidence.note: US adult survey. Ever-used wireless access is not a majority-of-traffic measure and is not global coverage.

reference.criterion: Learners can ordinarily obtain educational content through wireless Internet access.
reference.rationale: iTunes U distributed university material in 2007; contemporary wireless access and connected portable computers supplied the delivery route. This is an availability/distribution claim, not a claim that every course or school has discarded physical books.
